### 1. Trip Summary

* **Dates:** 1 October 2026 – 7 October 2026 (Note: Your dates span **7 calendar days / 6 nights**, starting with an early arrival and ending with a late-night departure).
* **Entry / Exit:** Arrive at Tokyo Narita (NRT) at 06:00 / Depart from Kansai International (KIX) at 23:30.
* **Route:** Tokyo (2 nights) → Kyoto (2 nights) → Osaka (2 nights, with a day trip to Hiroshima & Miyajima).
* **Pace:** Moderate. To keep the pace realistic and avoid packing/unpacking daily, Hiroshima is included as a high-speed Shinkansen day trip using Osaka as the hotel base.

---

### 2. Day-by-Day Itinerary

#### Day 1 (1 Oct 2026): Arrival & Historic Tokyo
* **Morning:** Land at Narita Airport (06:00). Clear customs, forward large luggage to your Kyoto hotel via airport luggage forwarding (*Ta-Q-Bin*) if desired, and take the **JR Narita Express (N'EX)** to Tokyo Station (approx. 60 min). Drop day bags at your hotel.
* **Afternoon:** Head to **Asakusa**. Walk through the Kaminarimon gate, browse Nakamise-dori, and visit **Senso-ji Temple**. Stroll along the Sumida River toward Tokyo Skytree for exterior views.
* **Evening:** Explore the neon alleys of **Ueno** or **Akihabara**.
* **Vegan Dining Recommendation:**
  * *Lunch:* **T’s Tantan** (inside the JR ticket gates at Tokyo Station or Ueno Station) — famous 100% plant-based ramen and gyoza.
  * *Dinner:* **Vegan Ramen Uzu Tokyo** (Toyosu area, reservation recommended) or **Ain Soph. Soar / Ain Soph. Journey** (plant-based Japanese fusion and pancakes).

#### Day 2 (2 Oct 2026): Modern Tokyo (Shibuya & Shinjuku)
* **Morning:** Visit **Meiji Jingu Shrine** in the forested heart of the city. Walk through Harajuku’s Takeshita Street to Omotesando.
* **Afternoon:** Head to **Shibuya**. Cross the iconic **Shibuya Crossing**, see the Hachiko statue, and take in the view from the open-air deck at **Shibuya Sky** (advance ticket booking required).
* **Evening:** Walk through Shinjuku’s **Omoide Yokocho** or observe the city skyline from the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks.
* **Vegan Dining Recommendation:**
  * *Lunch:* **Brown Rice by Neal's Yard Remedies** (Omotesando) — refined traditional set meals (*teishoku*) using seasonal, plant-based ingredients.
  * *Dinner:* **Ain Soph. Journey** (Shinjuku) or **Izakaya Masaka** (located in Shibuya PARCO basement; serves vegan karaage and izakaya-style dishes).

#### Day 3 (3 Oct 2026): High-Speed Rail to Kyoto & Higashiyama
* **Morning:** Take the **Tokaido Shinkansen (Nozomi)** from Tokyo Station to Kyoto Station (approx. 2 hours 15 minutes). Check into your hotel or store luggage.
* **Afternoon:** Take the Keihan line to **Fushimi Inari Taisha**; hike through the thousands of vermilion *torii* gates. Return to central Kyoto and wander the preserved stone streets of **Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka** up to **Kiyomizu-dera**.
* **Evening:** Walk through the historic **Gion** entertainment district along the Shirakawa canal.
* **Vegan Dining Recommendation:**
  * *Lunch:* **Veg Out** (near Shichijo Station along the Kamogawa River) — vegan grain bowls, paninis, and coffee.
  * *Dinner:* **Ain Soph. Journey Kyoto** (near Kawaramachi) or **TowZen** (specializes in rich vegan soymilk ramen).

#### Day 4 (4 Oct 2026): Western Kyoto & Bamboo Groves
* **Morning:** Take the JR San-in (Sagano) Line to **Arashiyama**. Arrive early to walk through the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before crowds peak, then visit **Tenryu-ji Temple** with its UNESCO Zen landscape garden.
* **Afternoon:** Head by bus or Randen tram to **Kinkaku-ji** (The Golden Pavilion). Spend the late afternoon sitting by the **Kamo River**.
* **Evening:** Browse the food stalls and shops in **Nishiki Market** (note: double-check ingredients here, as many traditional snacks contain fish stock).
* **Vegan Dining Recommendation:**
  * *Lunch:* **Shigetsu** (inside Tenryu-ji temple) — authentic multi-course Zen Buddhist vegetarian temple cuisine (*shojin ryori*). Must be reserved online in advance; naturally 100% vegan.
  * *Dinner:* **Mumokuteki Cafe** (central Kyoto) — casual, hearty vegan set menus, curries, and ramen.

#### Day 5 (5 Oct 2026): Day Trip to Hiroshima & Miyajima (Base Transfer to Osaka)
* **Morning:** Forward main bags or take the morning train to Osaka (JR Special Rapid, 30 min) to drop bags at an Osaka hotel near Shin-Osaka or Namba. Board the **Sanyo Shinkansen** from Shin-Osaka to Hiroshima Station (approx. 1 hour 25 minutes).
* **Mid-Day:** Take the tram/ferry to **Miyajima** to see the floating torii gate of **Itsukushima Shrine** and friendly wild deer.
* **Afternoon:** Return to central Hiroshima. Visit the **Peace Memorial Park**, the **Atomic Bomb Dome**, and the **Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum**.
* **Evening:** Shinkansen back to Osaka.
* **Vegan Dining Recommendation:**
  * *Lunch/Dinner in Hiroshima:* **Nagataya** (near the Peace Park) — offers a separate, dedicated vegetarian/vegan Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki cooked with vegan sauce and separate utensils.
  * *Late Dinner in Osaka:* **Paprika Shokudo Vegan** (Shin-sai-bashi) — fully organic, plant-based tavern serving vegan versions of Japanese comfort dishes.

#### Day 6 (6 Oct 2026): Vibrant Osaka
* **Morning:** Visit **Osaka Castle** and walk the surrounding moat gardens.
* **Afternoon:** Head to the retro district of **Shinsekai** to see the Tsutenkaku Tower. Walk up through the **Namba Parks** architectural complex.
* **Evening:** Explore **Dotonbori**. See the neon Glico Running Man sign and experience Osaka’s bustling evening atmosphere.
* **Vegan Dining Recommendation:**
  * *Lunch:* **Mercy Vegan Factory** (near Osaka Castle) — plant-based lunch sets and vegan baked goods.
  * *Dinner:* **OKO - Funky Vegetarian Okonomiyaki** (Namba/Shinsaibashi) — casual spot with custom vegan okonomiyaki and yakisoba.

#### Day 7 (7 Oct 2026): Osaka & Evening Departure
* **Morning:** Check out and leave bags with hotel reception. Visit the **Umeda Sky Building** for 360-degree views of Osaka from the Floating Garden Observatory.
* **Afternoon:** Do last-minute souvenir and gift shopping in the **Grand Front Osaka** or **Umeda** underground malls.
* **Evening:** Retrieve bags and board the **JR Haruka Express** directly to Kansai International Airport (approx. 50 minutes from Tennoji or 70 minutes from Shin-Osaka). 
* **Airport arrival:** Aim to arrive at KIX by 20:30 (3 hours before your 23:30 departure).
* **Vegan Dining Recommendation:**
  * *Lunch:* **Green Earth** (Honmachi) — one of Osaka’s oldest vegan cafes, known for hearty grain-and-soy patties and seasonal wraps.
  * *Airport Note:* Vegan choices airside at KIX are limited; purchase plant-based snacks, onigiri (e.g., plain salted *shio* or pickled plum *ume*), or bakery goods in Osaka city prior to boarding the train.

---

### 3. Transport & Pass Recommendation

* **7-Day Whole-Japan JR Pass:** **Not recommended.**
  * *Why:* Following JR's massive October 2023 price hike, a 7-day National Pass costs ¥50,000. Your individual routes (Tokyo → Kyoto = ~¥14,000; Shin-Osaka → Hiroshima RT = ~¥21,500; Airport express trains = ~¥5,000) total approximately **¥40,500**. Buying individual tickets is significantly cheaper and allows you to ride the faster *Nozomi* and *Mizuho* trains without an added surcharge fee.
* **Recommended Strategy:**
  1. **Tokyo to Kyoto:** Buy a point-to-point one-way ticket on the **Tokaido Shinkansen (Nozomi)**.
  2. **JR Kansai-Hiroshima Area Pass (5-Day):** **Highly recommended.** 
     * Cost: ¥17,000.
     * Coverage: Covers the round-trip Shinkansen between Shin-Osaka and Hiroshima, the JR West ferry to Miyajima, local JR trains in Kansai, and the **Kansai Airport Express "Haruka"** to KIX on Day 7. The round-trip train ride to Hiroshima alone costs over ¥21,000, meaning this regional pass pays for itself on that single day trip.
  3. **Local Travel:** Use an IC Card (Suica/Pasmo/ICOCA on your smartphone wallet) for intra-city subways, buses, and private rail lines.

---

### 4. Dietary Notes for Vegans in Japan

* **The "Dashi" Challenge:** Traditional Japanese cuisine relies heavily on *dashi* (bonito fish flake broth), which is often present in items that appear vegetarian (miso soup, dipping sauces, tofu dressings, and tamagoyaki).
* **How to Order:**
  * Carry a Japanese dietary card explicitly stating your requirements:
    * *"Watashi wa bīgan desu. Niku, sakana, dashi, tamago, nyūseihin o taberaremasen."* (I am vegan. I cannot eat meat, fish, fish broth, eggs, or dairy products).
* **Convenience Stores (Konbini):** Look for *Umeboshi* (pickled plum) or plain salted (*Shio*) *onigiri* (rice balls). Read labels carefully, as seaweed (*nori*) is sometimes seasoned with fish sauce or bonito extracts.
* **Essential Tool:** Download the **HappyCow** app. It is indispensable in Japan for identifying strictly vegan, vegetarian, or accommodating restaurants nearby.

---

### 5. Missing Information & Caveats

* **Date Clarification:** Your prompt requested a "6-day trip," but your flight window (1 Oct 06:00 to 7 Oct 23:30) encompasses **7 full daytime periods**. This itinerary utilizes all 7 days to make the Hiroshima excursion feasible.
* **Hiroshima Day Trip Fatigue:** Day 5 involves roughly 3–3.5 hours of round-trip train travel plus local ferries. If you prefer a slower, more immersive vacation, skip Hiroshima and spend that day taking a day trip to **Nara** or enjoying a relaxed second day in Kyoto.
* **Train Bookings & Oversized Baggage:** Shinkansen seats with oversized baggage space (total dimensions > 160 cm up to 250 cm) require advance reservations by law. If travelling with standard carry-on suitcases, this is not required.
* **Luggage Transfer:** Using a luggage forwarding service (*Ta-Q-Bin*) from Tokyo to Kyoto makes navigating crowded train stations with bags significantly easier.
